components.note: 歹 (death/bad) — 残 relates to damage, destruction, and injury.
戋 (jiān) gives a sound distantly related to cán, having drifted apart over time.
Wine — the original sense described the strong taste of wine.
Gives the sound gào, related to kù but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他对待俘虏的手段非常残酷。
example.pinyin: Tā duìdài fúlǔ de shǒuduàn fēicháng cánkù.
example.english: The way he treated prisoners was extremely cruel.
example.fact: The Roman Colosseum, completed in 80 AD, could hold an estimated 50,000 to 80,000 spectators who came to watch gladiatorial combat and staged animal hunts. Beneath the arena floor, a network of tunnels and lift mechanisms called the hypogeum let animals and fighters appear suddenly through trapdoors. Archaeologists estimate that hundreds of thousands of animals were killed there over the centuries of its use.

meanings: long-term task to which one devotes oneself

components.note: 亻 (person) — 使 involves a person carrying out a task.
吏 (a government official) — 使 originally referred to an official sent to carry out orders, giving rise to the meaning 'to make someone do something' or 'to use.'
令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'

example.hanzi: 他把保护环境当作自己的使命。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ bǎohù huánjìng dàngzuò zìjǐ de shǐmìng.
example.english: He treats protecting the environment as his mission.
example.fact: NASA's Voyager 1 probe, launched in 1977 on a mission to study the outer planets, has now traveled farther from Earth than any human-made object — over 24 billion kilometers as of the 2020s. It crossed into interstellar space in 2012 and still sends back data using a radio transmitter with less power than a refrigerator light bulb, a signal that takes over 22 hours to reach Earth.

components.note: 辶 (walk/movement) — 返 describes the act of traveling.
反 (opposite, reversed) — walking 辶 in reverse 反 gave 返 its meaning 'to return.'
回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'

example.hanzi: 飞机因为天气原因返回了机场。
example.pinyin: Fēijī yīnwèi tiānqì yuányīn fǎnhuí le jīchǎng.
example.english: The plane returned to the airport because of the weather.
example.fact: Monarch butterflies migrate up to 4,800 kilometers from Canada and the northern United States to the same forested mountains in central Mexico each winter, then return north in spring — even though no single butterfly completes the round trip, since the return leg is flown by their offspring several generations later. Scientists still do not fully understand how this multi-generational navigation is passed on.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 杯 names a cup, originally carved from wood.
不 (bù) shares the initial b- with bēi, though the rhyme has drifted from ù to ēi over time.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 请把那个杯子递给我。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ nàge bēizi dì gěi wǒ.
example.english: Please hand me that cup.
example.fact: The oldest known drinking vessels, dating back roughly 13,000 years, were discovered in a cave in Israel and were carved from the skulls of vultures, suggesting a ritual rather than everyday use. Ordinary cups made of clay only became widespread after the invention of pottery around 9,000 years ago, one of the technologies that let early humans store and transport liquids for the first time.

components.note: 宀 (a roof, house) sets the scene indoors.
丰 pictures a sharp blade pointing downward — a weapon brought inside the house gave 害 its meaning 'harm, injury.'
羊 (sheep) — 羞 pairs a sheep with the idea of something unsightly.
丑 (ugly, shameful) contributes to the character's form, giving 羞 its meaning 'ashamed, shy.'

example.hanzi: 小男孩见到陌生人就害羞地低下了头。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo nánhái jiàndào mòshēngrén jiù hàixiū de dīxià le tóu.
example.english: The little boy shyly lowered his head when he saw a stranger.
example.fact: Blushing, a common physical sign of shyness or embarrassment, is unique to humans among all animals — no other species has been shown to blush. Charles Darwin called it 'the most peculiar and most human of all expressions' in his 1872 book on emotion, noting that it happens involuntarily and cannot be produced or suppressed at will, which is part of why it is such a reliable social signal.

components.note: 帝 depicts an altar stand used for sacrificial offerings to the gods — the one who presides over such rites came to be known as 帝, 'supreme ruler, emperor.'
囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.

example.hanzi: 罗马帝国在其鼎盛时期统治了大片欧洲领土。
example.pinyin: Luómǎ dìguó zài qí dǐngshèng shíqī tǒngzhì le dàpiàn Ōuzhōu lǐngtǔ.
example.english: The Roman Empire ruled vast European territory at its height.
example.fact: At its greatest extent around 117 AD, the Roman Empire covered roughly 5 million square kilometers and governed an estimated 60 to 70 million people, close to a fifth of the world's population at the time. Its network of paved roads eventually stretched over 400,000 kilometers, engineered well enough that some sections remain in use as modern roadbeds today.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.
合 depicts a lid fitted closed over a container beneath it — two halves joining as one gave 合 its meaning 'to close, to unite, to match.'

example.hanzi: 这种场合应该穿得正式一些。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng chǎnghé yīnggāi chuān de zhèngshì yīxiē.
example.english: You should dress more formally for this kind of occasion.
example.fact: The tuxedo, now standard formalwear for many occasions, gets its English name from Tuxedo Park, a private club in New York state where it was reportedly first worn to a fall ball in 1886, breaking with the tailcoats then expected at such events. The style was itself adapted from a shorter smoking jacket popularized by the Prince of Wales in Britain.

components.note: 酉 (a wine jar) — the vessel holding the drink
氵 (liquid) — the wine itself inside the jar
米 (grain, especially husked rice) — 精's meaning 'refined, essence, spirit' relates to rice refined to its purest form.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 精 is pronounced jīng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.

example.hanzi: 医生用酒精给伤口消毒。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng yòng jiǔjīng gěi shāngkǒu xiāodú.
example.english: The doctor disinfected the wound with alcohol.
example.fact: Ethyl alcohol boils at 78.4 degrees Celsius, well below water's 100 degrees, which is exactly why distillation works: heating a fermented liquid lets the alcohol vaporize first and be collected separately. This same volatility is why rubbing alcohol feels cold on skin — as it evaporates quickly, it pulls heat away from the surface it touches.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.
五 places an X-shaped cross between two horizontal lines representing heaven and earth — in traditional cosmology, this was linked to the five elements that fill the space between.

example.hanzi: 我们星期五晚上一起去看电影吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xīngqīwǔ wǎnshang yìqǐ qù kàn diànyǐng ba.
example.english: Let's go watch a movie together on Friday night.
example.fact: The English word 'Friday' comes from Old English Frīgedæg, meaning 'day of Frigg,' the Norse goddess associated with love and fate — the same naming pattern that gave Thursday its link to Thor. In several unrelated cultures, including much of the Islamic and Jewish world, Friday or the transition into it carries special religious significance, marking the start of communal prayer or the Sabbath.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the sea or river being traveled through
斿 — a banner streaming in the wind, evoking free, drifting movement
氵 (water) — 泳 describes moving through water.
永 (yǒng) gives the sound — an exact match with 泳.
氵 (water) shows 池 relates to a body of water.
也 (yě) gives a sound distantly related to chí, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 夏天孩子们喜欢在游泳池里玩耍。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān háizimen xǐhuan zài yóuyǒngchí lǐ wánshuǎ.
example.english: In summer, children like playing in the swimming pool.
example.fact: The San Alfonso del Mar resort in Chile holds the record for the world's largest swimming pool, stretching over 1,000 meters long and holding about 250 million liters of filtered seawater. Because it is open to the ocean and unheated by comparison, its water is kept clear using a system that draws seawater in through a specially designed suction and filtration mechanism rather than conventional chlorination alone.

components.note: 山 (mountain) surrounds the character, setting the scene.
幺 (small, doubled here) shows tiny hidden niches within the mountainside, giving 幽 its meaning 'secluded, hidden, dark.'
火 (fire) — linked to ritual fires once used to try to communicate with spirits
彐 (jì) gives a sound distantly related to 灵's reading líng, having drifted apart considerably over time

example.hanzi: 村民们都说那座老房子里有幽灵。
example.pinyin: Cūnmínmen dōu shuō nà zuò lǎo fángzi lǐ yǒu yōulíng.
example.english: The villagers all say there's a ghost in that old house.
example.fact: A 2019 YouGov poll found that around 45 percent of Americans said they believe ghosts can interact with the living, a belief with roots across many cultures long before it took modern form. Scientists who study reported hauntings often point to infrasound — sound below the range of human hearing, sometimes produced by old building structures or machinery — as a physical explanation for feelings of unease or fleeting visual disturbances.

components.note: 木 (wood) — early models and molds were often carved from wood
莫 (mò) gives a sound close to 模's reading mó, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
土 (earth) — 型 originally related to a mold made of clay used for casting
刑 (xíng) gives the sound — 型 is also pronounced xíng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 工程师先做了一个建筑模型。
example.pinyin: Gōngchéngshī xiān zuò le yí gè jiànzhù móxíng.
example.english: The engineer first made a model of the building.
example.fact: Before large wind tunnels existed, engineers tested aircraft and building designs using scale models in smaller tunnels, a method still used today because full-size testing is often too costly or dangerous. The Wright brothers built their own 1.8-meter wind tunnel in 1901 and tested over 200 miniature wing shapes, data that proved more reliable than the aerodynamic tables available at the time and helped make their 1903 flight possible.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诡 relates to deceptive words or schemes.
危 (wēi) gives a sound distantly related to guǐ, having drifted apart over time.
异 (a simplified form of 異) depicts a person with upraised hands and an odd expression, suggesting something strange or different.

example.hanzi: 那栋废弃的房子看起来十分诡异。
example.pinyin: Nà dòng fèiqì de fángzi kàn qǐlai shífēn guǐyì.
example.english: That abandoned house looks really strange.
example.fact: The 'uncanny valley' is a term coined by roboticist Masahiro Mori in 1970 to describe the strange, unsettling feeling people get when a robot or animated figure looks almost — but not quite — human. Researchers have since traced part of this effect to subtle mismatches in facial movement timing, which the brain detects even when a viewer cannot consciously say what looks wrong.

components.note: 十 (here a straight vertical line) — 直 pictures something drawn perfectly straight.
目 (eye) — looking directly and steadily with the eye gave 直 its meaning 'straight' or 'direct.'
讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō

example.hanzi: 你有什么想法就直说吧，别客气。
example.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme xiǎngfǎ jiù zhíshuō ba, bié kèqi.
example.english: If you have any thoughts, just say them directly, don't be polite about it.
example.fact: Cultures vary widely in how much they value direct versus indirect speech — linguistic anthropologists often cite Dutch and German conversational norms as unusually blunt by international standards, while many East Asian and Middle Eastern communication styles favor softer, more indirect phrasing to preserve social harmony. Researchers studying workplace communication have found that misjudging this cultural gap is one of the most common sources of misunderstanding in international business teams.

components.note: 冫 (water) — 准 originally referred to a carpenter's level using water to check flatness, extended to 'standard, accurate, level.'
隹 (zhuī) gives a sound hint — 准 is pronounced zhǔn, sharing the base sound though the vowel and tone differ somewhat.
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

example.hanzi: 他每次开会都很准时。
example.pinyin: Tā měicì kāihuì dōu hěn zhǔnshí.
example.english: He is always punctual for meetings.
example.fact: Japan's Shinkansen bullet trains have an average delay of less than one minute per year across the entire network, a punctuality record often cited as the best of any major rail system in the world. Part of the reason is structural: dedicated track separate from freight and local trains removes most of the scheduling conflicts that cause delays elsewhere.

components.note: 画 depicts a picture set within a frame — the traditional form 畫 additionally showed a hand holding a brush above it.
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 电影里那个爆炸的画面让人印象深刻。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ nàge bàozhà de huàmiàn ràng rén yìnxiàng shēnkè.
example.english: That explosion scene in the movie left a deep impression.
example.fact: Early film ran at 16 to 18 frames per second, but the industry settled on 24 frames per second in the late 1920s specifically to accommodate the new technology of synchronized sound, since that speed matched well with the film stock and audio equipment of the era. Modern digital cameras can capture thousands of frames per second, which is how ultra-slow-motion footage of events like a hummingbird's wingbeat becomes possible.

components.note: 阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.

example.hanzi: 这位部长负责教育政策。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi bùzhǎng fùzé jiàoyù zhèngcè.
example.english: This minister is responsible for education policy.
example.fact: William Pitt the Younger became Britain's youngest prime minister in 1783 at just 24 years old, a record that still stands more than two centuries later. He went on to lead the country through the French Revolutionary Wars, serving two separate terms totaling almost two decades.

components.note: The character traces the front view of an ox's head, with the top stroke and crossing lines representing its curved horns and ears.
冂 traces the outer outline of a cut of meat.
仌 depicts the muscle fibers or ribs inside, together forming a picture of a piece of meat.

example.hanzi: 妈妈今天买了一些牛肉做晚饭。
example.pinyin: Māma jīntiān mǎi le yìxiē niúròu zuò wǎnfàn.
example.english: Mom bought some beef today to make dinner.
example.fact: Cattle require far more land, water, and feed per calorie produced than crops or poultry, which is why beef has one of the largest environmental footprints of any common food — producing it generates several times more greenhouse gas per kilogram than chicken or pork. A single adult cow can also belch out over 100 kilograms of methane a year as part of its digestion, a byproduct of the specialized four-chambered stomach that lets it break down tough plant fiber.

components.note: A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
阝 (hill) — 降 originally related to coming down a hill or slope
夅 (jiàng) gives the sound — an exact match with 降's reading jiàng

example.hanzi: 今年公司的销售额出现了明显下降。
example.pinyin: Jīnnián gōngsī de xiāoshòu'é chūxiàn le míngxiǎn xiàjiàng.
example.english: The company's sales showed a clear decline this year.
example.fact: The global population of monarch butterflies overwintering in Mexico has dropped by more than 80 percent since the mid-1990s, largely due to the loss of milkweed habitat along their migration route in the United States. Conservationists now track the decline yearly by measuring the total forest area the butterflies occupy each winter, since counting individual insects directly is impractical.

components.note: 丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
疋 — a person walking, shown pausing and looking back uncertainly
矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating

example.hanzi: 警察发现了一个可疑的包裹。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá fāxiàn le yí gè kěyí de bāoguǒ.
example.english: The police found a suspicious package.
example.fact: Trained detection dogs can identify certain explosives at concentrations as low as parts per trillion, a sensitivity far beyond most electronic sensors, because a dog's nose contains up to 300 million olfactory receptors compared to roughly 6 million in a human nose. This is why airports and security checkpoints worldwide still rely on dogs to flag suspicious luggage even alongside advanced scanning equipment.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恶 relates to an evil or malicious state of heart/mind
亚 (yà) gives a sound distantly related to 恶's reading è, having drifted apart over time
林 here depicts eyes shut in sleep, not its usual meaning 'forest.'
夕 (evening, night) — sleeping at night is when dreams occur, giving 梦 its meaning 'dream.'

example.hanzi: 他昨晚做了一个可怕的恶梦。
example.pinyin: Tā zuówǎn zuò le yí gè kěpà de èmèng.
example.english: He had a terrible nightmare last night.
example.fact: Nightmares occur almost exclusively during REM sleep, the stage in which the brain is highly active and most vivid dreaming happens, typically in the later part of the night when REM periods grow longer. Researchers have found that people who are sleep-deprived and then allowed to sleep normally often experience 'REM rebound,' a temporary surge in REM sleep that can make nightmares more frequent for a night or two.

components.note: 亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'
刂 (knife) — 制 relates to cutting and shaping, and by extension, to making or controlling something.
巾 (jīn) gives a hint of the sound — 制 is pronounced zhì, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 请帮我复制这份文件。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ fùzhì zhè fèn wénjiàn.
example.english: Please help me copy this document.
example.fact: The Gutenberg printing press, developed around 1440, was the first technology to make mass-copying of text practical, and it is estimated to have produced more books in its first 50 years than European scribes had copied by hand in the previous thousand. A single press could turn out around 3,600 pages a day, compared to a handful produced by a scribe working manually.

meanings: (of a body part) to be painful
(of a person) to be in pain

components.note: 疒 (sickness) shows 疼 relates to pain or discomfort.
冬 (dōng) gives a sound close to téng, sharing a similar consonant sound.
疒 (sickness) — 痛 relates to physical pain or illness
甬 (yǒng) gives a sound distantly related to 痛's reading tòng, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 手术后他的伤口疼痛了好几天。
example.pinyin: Shǒushù hòu tā de shāngkǒu téngtòng le hǎo jǐ tiān.
example.english: His wound was painful for several days after the surgery.
example.fact: Pain signals travel from the body to the brain along nerve fibers at very different speeds depending on type: sharp, immediate pain travels along fast A-delta fibers at up to 30 meters per second, while the duller, longer-lasting ache that follows travels along slower C fibers at under 2 meters per second. This is part of why a stubbed toe often produces a quick sharp pain followed, a moment later, by a throbbing one.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 摄 describes taking hold of or capturing something, as in taking a photograph.
聂 (niè) gives a sound distantly related to shè's reading, having drifted apart over time.
彡 (fine lines) — suggests light and shadow, relating to 影's meaning 'shadow, image.'
景 (jǐng) gives a sound hint — 影 is pronounced yǐng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢用旅行的机会练习摄影。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yòng lǔxíng de jīhuì liànxí shèyǐng.
example.english: He likes to use travel opportunities to practice photography.
example.fact: The first permanent photograph was made by Joseph Nicéphore Niépce in 1826 or 1827, showing a rooftop view outside his window in France, and it required an exposure time of about eight hours. By comparison, a modern smartphone camera can capture and process a photo in a fraction of a second, a difference of many orders of magnitude in just under two centuries.

components.note: 门 (door) frames the scene.
人 (person) glimpsed briefly inside, giving 闪 its meaning 'to flash, to dodge quickly.'
电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'

example.hanzi: 一道闪电划过漆黑的夜空。
example.pinyin: Yī dào shǎndiàn huàguò qīhēi de yèkōng.
example.english: A bolt of lightning cut across the pitch-black night sky.
example.fact: A single lightning bolt can reach temperatures of about 30,000 Kelvin, roughly five times hotter than the surface of the sun, which is what causes the rapid expansion of air that produces thunder. Earth experiences an estimated 8 million lightning strikes every day, most of them in tropical regions where warm, moist air fuels frequent thunderstorms.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 积 originally referred to grain piled up and stored
只 (zhǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 积's reading jī, having drifted apart over time
木 (wood) — 极 originally named the ridgepole, the highest beam of a roof, extended to 'extreme, utmost.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 极 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 他对新工作表现得非常积极。
example.pinyin: Tā duì xīn gōngzuò biǎoxiàn de fēicháng jījí.
example.english: He is very positive and proactive about his new job.
example.fact: Psychologist Martin Seligman's research in the 1990s helped found the field of positive psychology, showing that actively cultivating optimism and engagement, rather than just treating mental illness, measurably improves people's well-being and resilience. His studies found that people who kept a simple daily record of things that went well reported higher happiness levels weeks later, even after they stopped the exercise.

components.note: 亻 (person) — represents a human figure.

叚 depicts borrowing or handing something over — a person who is not genuine, or something borrowed rather than real, gave 假 its meaning 'false, fake' (and, for a break from routine, 'vacation, leave.')
釆 (to distinguish/sort) — 释 relates to sorting out and clarifying, i.e. 'to explain'
睪 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to 释's reading shì, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 他因为表现良好提前获得了假释。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi biǎoxiàn liánghǎo tíqián huòdé le jiǎshì.
example.english: He was granted early parole for good behavior.
example.fact: The modern parole system traces back to Alexander Maconochie, a British naval officer who ran a penal colony on Norfolk Island off Australia in the 1840s and introduced a 'mark system' letting prisoners earn early release through good conduct and work, rather than serving a fixed sentence regardless of behavior. His ideas influenced prison reform across Britain, Ireland, and eventually the United States.

components.note: 巴 traces the coiled body of a snake in its earliest oracle-bone forms. The character was later borrowed for its sound alone in place names and transliterations, as in this one, unrelated to its original picture.
其 (qí) echoes a sound distantly related to sī, the two having drifted apart over the centuries.
斤 (axe) — 斯 originally meant 'to split, to chop,' later extended to 'this' and, as here, used purely for its sound in transliterating foreign names.

example.hanzi: 巴斯是英国西南部一座著名的古城。
example.pinyin: Bāsī shì Yīngguó xīnánbù yí zuò zhùmíng de gǔchéng.
example.english: Bath is a famous ancient city in southwest England.
example.fact: The city of Bath is named for its natural hot springs, the only ones in Britain, which the Romans channeled into an elaborate bathing complex around 70 AD that still stands today as the Roman Baths. The springs draw water heated deep underground that resurfaces at about 46 degrees Celsius, having taken an estimated 10,000 years to complete its journey through the rock.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 评 relates to speaking judgments or opinions about something
平 (píng) gives the sound — an exact match with 评's reading píng
亻 (person) — 估 describes a person making a judgment or guess.
古 (gǔ) gives a sound close to gū, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 专家对这个项目的风险进行了评估。
example.pinyin: Zhuānjiā duì zhège xiàngmù de fēngxiǎn jìnxíng le pínggū.
example.english: Experts carried out a risk assessment of this project.
example.fact: The Richter scale, long used to assess earthquake magnitude, is logarithmic, meaning each whole-number increase represents a tenfold rise in measured amplitude and roughly 31 times more released energy. Because of this, seismologists now more often rely on the moment magnitude scale for large earthquakes, which better assesses total energy release for the biggest, most damaging events.

components.note: 角 (horn) — 解 pictures removing a part of an animal.
牛 (ox) — together with a knife cutting between horn and ox, 解 pictures separating something into parts, giving its meaning 'to untie' or 'to explain.'
阝 (a mound/settlement) — represents a city or town.
余 (surplus, remainder) — the leftover waste a city produces, which must be cleared away, giving 除 its meaning 'to remove, eliminate.'

example.hanzi: 政府决定解除对该地区的旅行限制。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ juédìng jiěchú duì gāi dìqū de lǔxíng xiànzhì.
example.english: The government decided to lift travel restrictions on the region.
example.fact: The United States lifted its arms embargo against Vietnam in 2016, more than 40 years after the end of the Vietnam War, as part of a broader normalization of relations between the two countries. Embargoes of this kind are typically removed gradually, often tied to specific diplomatic or human rights benchmarks rather than a single decision.

components.note: A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
广 (shelter) pictures a roofed building.
车 (cart) sits inside, together giving 库 its meaning 'storehouse, warehouse.'

example.hanzi: 他把车停在车库里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ chē tíng zài chēkù lǐ.
example.english: He parked the car in the garage.
example.fact: The Hewlett-Packard company was founded in a one-car garage in Palo Alto in 1939 by Bill Hewlett and David Packard, working with just $538 in starting capital. That garage is now a California Historical Landmark, often called the symbolic birthplace of Silicon Valley, since it set a pattern later followed by companies like Apple and Google, which also started in garages.

components.note: 辶 (to walk, movement) — 通 relates to passing through or getting somewhere.
甬 (yǒng) gives a hint of the sound — 通 is pronounced tōng, a connection that has shifted over time.
讠 (speech) — 讯 relates to asking questions and gathering information through words.
卂 (xùn) is an exact match for the sound of 讯.

example.hanzi: 这家公司主要从事通讯设备的生产。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhǔyào cóngshì tōngxùn shèbèi de shēngchǎn.
example.english: This company mainly produces communications equipment.
example.fact: The first transatlantic telegraph cable, completed in 1858, cut communication time between North America and Europe from about ten days by ship to just minutes, though the cable itself failed after only a few weeks due to a technical fault. A more durable cable was successfully laid in 1866, permanently transforming global communications and finance by allowing near-instant transatlantic messages.

components.note: 日 (sun) — represents the sun.
十 depicts the first rays of sunlight appearing low on the horizon — together with 日 (sun) giving 早 its meaning 'early, morning.'
宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'

example.hanzi: 他每天早上都会跟邻居说一声早安。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang dōu huì gēn línjū shuō yìshēng zǎo'ān.
example.english: Every morning he greets his neighbor with a 'good morning.'
example.fact: Human circadian rhythms, which govern when we naturally wake and feel alert, are regulated by a small cluster of about 20,000 neurons in the brain called the suprachiasmatic nucleus, which resets daily based on light hitting the eyes. This is why morning sunlight exposure is one of the most effective tools for adjusting sleep schedules, including recovering from jet lag.

components.note: 身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.

后 originally pictured a ruler seated with mouth open, issuing a decree — its earliest meaning was 'monarch, queen.' The character was later reused as the simplified form of 後 (behind, after), the sense intended here, a meaning unrelated to its original picture.

example.hanzi: 他身后留下了一笔可观的财产。
example.pinyin: Tā shēnhòu liúxià le yì bǐ kěguān de cáichǎn.
example.english: He left behind a considerable fortune after his death.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptian pharaohs were buried with elaborate provisions meant to last for the afterlife, including furniture, food, and in some cases entire boats, based on a belief that the journey continued after death. Tutankhamun's tomb, discovered largely intact in 1922, contained over 5,000 objects, giving archaeologists an unusually complete picture of what a ruler was thought to need beyond life.

components.note: 日 (sun) — represents the sun.
十 depicts the first rays of sunlight appearing low on the horizon — together with 日 (sun) giving 早 its meaning 'early, morning.'
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 他没时间吃早点就出门了。
example.pinyin: Tā méi shíjiān chī zǎodiǎn jiù chūmén le.
example.english: He left the house without time to eat breakfast.
example.fact: The word 'breakfast' literally describes breaking an overnight fast, and for most of human history, the meal was far less standardized than it is today — medieval European physicians sometimes even discouraged eating first thing in the morning, believing it disrupted digestion. It only became a widely promoted, regular meal in the 19th century, partly through advertising campaigns for new packaged foods like breakfast cereal.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — 盘 names a flat dish or tray.
般 (bān) gives a sound distantly related to pán, having drifted apart over time.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 服务员端来了一盘子水果。
example.pinyin: Fúwùyuán duān lái le yì pánzi shuǐguǒ.
example.english: The waiter brought over a plate of fruit.
example.fact: Blue and white porcelain plates, closely associated with Chinese ceramics, reached peak popularity during the Yuan and Ming dynasties starting in the 14th century, using cobalt pigment imported along trade routes from Persia. European potters spent centuries trying to replicate true porcelain's hard, translucent quality, only succeeding after Johann Friedrich Böttger's breakthrough in Saxony in 1708.

meanings: comes at the end of the sentence to indicate a strong degree

components.note: 目 (eye) relates to 着's senses of 'to look at, to touch, to attach to' — something coming into view or into contact.
The upper portion descends from 著 (zhù), the character 着 evolved from as a simplified variant; its pronunciation has since split into zhe, zháo, and zhāo depending on use.
口 (mouth) — relates to 呢's role as a spoken sentence particle.
尼 (ní) provides the base sound, though 呢 is usually spoken with a neutral, unstressed tone.

example.hanzi: 这道题他其实明白着呢。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào tí tā qíshí míngbai zhe ne.
example.english: He actually understands this problem quite well.
example.fact: Emphatic sentence particles that intensify a statement appear in many of the world's languages, not just Chinese — Japanese uses particles like 'yo' and 'zo' for a similar effect, and colloquial German relies heavily on 'doch' and 'ja' to shade the emotional weight of a sentence. Linguists classify these as modal particles, since they change how strongly or in what tone a statement is meant, without altering its literal content.

components.note: 女 (woman) — depicts a wife in the traditional image behind this character.
口 (mouth/words) — the wife following her husband's spoken words gave 如 its meaning of 'as, like, if.'
凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'

example.hanzi: 他的经历如同一部精彩的小说。
example.pinyin: Tā de jīnglì rútóng yí bù jīngcǎi de xiǎoshuō.
example.english: His experiences are just like an exciting novel.
example.fact: The chambered nautilus grows its spiral shell in a logarithmic pattern, adding new, proportionally larger chambers as it ages while always maintaining the same overall shape — a growth pattern often compared to certain hurricanes and galaxies because all three follow similar spiral mathematics. This is why the nautilus shell is a favorite classroom example for demonstrating logarithmic spirals found throughout nature.

components.note: 纟 (thread/silk) — 给 originally related to supplying thread or material, later broadening to mean 'to give.'
合 (hé) gives a hint of the sound — 给 is pronounced gěi, a connection that has shifted over time.
予 depicts two hands passing an object between them, one releasing and one receiving — a simple picture of handing something over that gave 予 its meaning 'to give, to bestow.'

example.hanzi: 公司决定给予员工额外的奖金。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī juédìng jǐyǔ yuángōng éwài de jiǎngjīn.
example.english: The company decided to give employees an extra bonus.
example.fact: The Nobel Prizes, among the most prestigious awards given for contributions to humanity, were established through the 1895 will of Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel, who left over 94 percent of his fortune to fund them — reportedly influenced by seeing himself mistakenly described in an obituary as a 'merchant of death' for inventing dynamite. The physics, chemistry, and medicine prizes have been awarded almost every year since 1901.

components.note: 廴 (to move forward, extend) — 建 relates to constructing or setting something up over an extended process.
聿 (yù) gives a hint of the sound — 建 is pronounced jiàn, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 造's meaning 'to make, build,' an action carried through to completion.
告 (gào) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zào.

example.hanzi: 工人们正在建造一座新桥。
example.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài jiànzào yí zuò xīn qiáo.
example.english: The workers are building a new bridge.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China was not built as a single continuous project but assembled and rebuilt over roughly 2,000 years by successive dynasties, with the best-preserved sections dating to the Ming dynasty starting in the 14th century. Combining all its branches and sections, surveys have measured the wall's total length at more than 21,000 kilometers, far longer than the commonly cited figure for any single stretch.

components.note: The 曲-shaped top pictures a bundle of bamboo strips, an ancient book.
八 below pictures two hands supporting the book, giving 典 its meaning 'classic text, standard.'
土 (earth) — 型 originally related to a mold made of clay used for casting
刑 (xíng) gives the sound — 型 is also pronounced xíng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 这是一个典型的误解案例。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè diǎnxíng de wùjiě ànlì.
example.english: This is a typical case of misunderstanding.
example.fact: In biology, a 'type specimen' is the single physical example — often a preserved animal or plant — permanently designated as the official reference for a species' name, kept in a museum collection so scientists can compare future finds against it. Carl Linnaeus, who founded the modern system of naming species in the 18th century, based many of his original type specimens on collections that are still preserved today.

example.hanzi: 他只是呵呵地笑了两声，没有说话。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǐshì hēhē de xiào le liǎng shēng, méiyǒu shuōhuà.
example.english: He just chuckled softly and didn't say anything.
example.fact: Laughter is thought to have evolved long before spoken language, since chimpanzees and other great apes produce a breathy, panting vocalization during play that researchers consider an evolutionary precursor to human laughing. Human laughter itself splits into distinct types studied by acoustic researchers, ranging from voiced, song-like laughs to unvoiced grunts and chuckles, each carrying different social signals.

components.note: 石 (rock/stone) — 破 relates to breaking, as a rock can be broken
皮 (pí) gives a loose sound connection to 破's reading pò
厂 (chǎng) gives a hint of the sound — 产 is pronounced chǎn, nearly identical apart from the final consonant.

example.hanzi: 那家公司因为经营不善宣布破产。
example.pinyin: Nà jiā gōngsī yīnwèi jīngyíng bùshàn xuānbù pòchǎn.
example.english: That company declared bankruptcy due to poor management.
example.fact: The word 'bankrupt' comes from the Italian banca rotta, meaning 'broken bench,' referring to the practice in medieval Italy of physically breaking a money-lender's table in the marketplace when he could not pay his debts. Modern bankruptcy law traces much of its structure to English statutes from the 16th century, which were originally aimed at punishing debtors rather than helping them recover.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 查 originally named a wooden raft used to ford or inspect a river, a sense that extended over time to 'to examine, to investigate.'
旦 (dàn) echoes a sound distantly related to chá, the two having drifted apart considerably over time.
手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'

example.hanzi: 请帮我查看一下这个数据。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ chákàn yíxià zhège shùjù.
example.english: Please help me check this data.
example.fact: The Voyager Golden Record, launched into space in 1977, was designed so that a sufficiently advanced civilization could check its contents using instructions etched onto its cover, including a diagram showing how to build a device to play it and images decoded pixel by pixel. It carried sounds and images meant to represent life and culture on Earth to whoever might one day examine it.

components.note: 亻 (person) shows 伪 describes something false or counterfeit, often about people's actions or claims.
为 (wéi) gives a sound very close to wěi, differing mainly in tone.
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 造's meaning 'to make, build,' an action carried through to completion.
告 (gào) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zào.

example.hanzi: 有人伪造了他的签名。
example.pinyin: Yǒu rén wěizào le tā de qiānmíng.
example.english: Someone forged his signature.
example.fact: Han van Meegeren, a Dutch painter active in the 1930s and 40s, forged paintings so convincingly attributed to Johannes Vermeer that top art experts of the era authenticated them as genuine, and one was even sold to a senior Nazi official during World War II. Van Meegeren was only caught after the war, when he had to prove the painting was his own forgery to avoid a treason charge for selling Dutch cultural heritage to the enemy.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 冠军选手最后一个出场。
example.pinyin: Guànjūn xuǎnshǒu zuìhòu yí gè chūchǎng.
example.english: The champion athlete came out last.
example.fact: At the Olympic Games opening ceremony, the host country's athletes traditionally enter the stadium last, a tradition formalized at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, while every other nation enters alphabetically according to the host country's language. This order is why viewers often see Greece, home of the ancient Olympics, enter first regardless of the host nation's alphabet.

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'
⺷ (sheep, related to 羊) — 义 relates to what is right or moral, linked to the idea of sacrificial sheep used in rituals of righteousness.
乂 (yì) gives the sound — 义 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这个基金会以帮助贫困儿童的名义筹款。
example.pinyin: Zhège jījīnhuì yǐ bāngzhù pínkùn értóng de míngyì chóukuǎn.
example.english: This foundation raises funds in the name of helping poor children.
example.fact: Many international charities operate under officially registered names that differ from their commonly known public name, a legal structure used to raise funds across borders while satisfying each country's separate registration and tax requirements. Regulatory bodies in most countries require charities to publicly disclose what percentage of donations raised in their name actually reaches program work versus administrative and fundraising costs.

meanings: in the middle of the night

components.note: 牛 (ox/cow) — cattle were used to help split or divide things such as firewood.
丷 depicts two small pieces splitting apart — giving 半 its meaning 'half.'
夕 (evening/night) — the darkness that has fallen
亻 (a person) — someone moving under cover of night

example.hanzi: 他半夜被一阵怪声吵醒了。
example.pinyin: Tā bànyè bèi yí zhèn guài shēng chǎo xǐng le.
example.english: He was woken up at midnight by a strange noise.
example.fact: The convention of starting a new calendar day at midnight rather than at sunrise or sunset, common in many older cultures, became standardized largely through the spread of mechanical clocks in medieval Europe, which could track time evenly through the night rather than relying on daylight. Astronomers, however, traditionally used a system where the day began at noon, a practice that persisted in some astronomical records until the early 20th century, since noon observations of the sun were far easier to make precisely.

components.note: 贝 (money) — gambling involves staking money.
者 (zhě) gives a sound distantly related to dǔ, having drifted apart over time.
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 他把所有的钱都输在了赌场里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ suǒyǒu de qián dōu shū zài le dǔchǎng lǐ.
example.english: He lost all his money at the casino.
example.fact: The word 'casino' comes from the Italian for 'little house,' originally referring to a small country villa or summer house used for social gatherings, long before it came to mean a gambling establishment. The Casino di Venezia, opened in Venice in 1638, is generally considered the oldest continuously run gambling house in the world.

components.note: 力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.

example.hanzi: 搬这个箱子需要很大的力气。
example.pinyin: Bān zhège xiāngzi xūyào hěn dà de lìqi.
example.english: Moving this box requires a lot of physical strength.
example.fact: The dung beetle can pull more than 1,000 times its own body weight, giving it, relative to size, one of the strongest grips of any animal on Earth, a feat researchers have linked to competition among males over mates. By comparison, most strength records among large animals, such as elephants, are far less impressive when scaled against body weight.
